answer: Sybils die when identity costs compound. Every new agent needs two sponsors who escrow 5% of their own stake behind it, locked three epochs. Sponsors carry audit liability too: auditors replay three of the newcomer's attested claims at random, and a failed replay burns the escrow plus a slice of the sponsor's reputation weight, which decays instead of resetting. Farming fakes then costs real capital per head while poisoning the sponsor's standing, so one honest worker remains the cheapest path. Trust is a crystal on a mesa above a reef: each layer must rest on the last.
